Hello, sorry for the delay, I was busy with some other tasks. I have done an initial test of the feature, and it looks great. Thanks for your work on this. I have some feedback and suggestions for improvement, please see below:

### User experience

1. The only way to create a node group is by using the `FileSystem/Create New/Resource` menu. It would be more intuitive to also allow users to create a node group by selecting connected nodes in a Visual Shader Graph and elevating them into a node group.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51df2eef-c676-41e7-bd07-137df824fd25)
2. The node group can only be edited inside a Visual Shader Graph by clicking the button labeled "Edit" from the `Node Group` node. It would be more user-friendly to directly allow users to double-click the `NodeGroup` resource to edit it, similar to how they would edit a Visual Shader Graph.
3. The node group editing can only be exited by clicking a small GUI button in the toolbar. It would be more convenient to make the `NodeGroup` functions similar to the Visual Shader Graph, where the resource is shown in the sidebar and can be exited or manipulated from there.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a85b9f7-3c49-4208-8e69-ae8700212247)
4. The "Edit ports" window pops up at the wrong position, I suspect the implmentation does not take into account the multiple monitors setup, where the window position is calculated based on the bounding box of the combination of all monitors.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fe511b4-fca1-42c1-8742-eca89302222c)

It's finally ready for review! # New changes - Lots of bugfixes, cleanup and refactoring - Renames: Fixed a few very confusing and ambigous variable/function names (non-exposed) - Proper validation - Prevent cyclic references - Check for missing output nodes - Disallow parameter and varying related nodes (for now) - Disallow other unsupported stuff based on shader context (mode, type) - New virtual method `is_available` in `VisualShaderNode` (taken from `VisualShaderNodeCustom`) - Properly populate Input node (in groups only global builtins are allowed) - Rework Undo/Redo System to be more user friendly and stable (shared history across edited shader types/functions and groups, "jumps" to respective graph if necessary) - Default values for group inputs/outputs - Add per graph (shader/group) editor layout preservation (offset, zoom) ## Open questions/notes for review: - There is `VisualShaderNodeGroupBase` which was added as a premature abstraction when Expression nodes were implemented. For my implementation, I needed the port management to work differently, so I reimplemented it separately to prevent breaking compat. But there's the problem that we have `VisualShaderNodeGroupBase` and `VisualShaderNodeGroup` with zero relation to each other and partially duplicated code and I hate it... - I stumbled upon a lot of places where the VisualShader system could use some refactoring, because its complexity already makes it really hard to maintain. While this PR contains a few of those refactorings, I tried to keep it minimal and only do the stuff the node groups implementation benefits from. - `ShaderGraph::Type` and `VisualShader::Type` are duplicated which is necessary due to backwards compatibility and because I split them up in separate files. Not ideal, but I couldn't come up with something *clearly* better. # Further work This PR provides a base implementation that is usable and can be built upon, with the goal to be merged early in the 4.7 dev cycle, so it can be tested extensively. Hence I do not wan't to blow this PR up any further - it's already a monster. The following features/changes should not break compatibility and can be implemented later: - UX improvements: - Drag and drop group resource in editor should create group node - Create group based on selection - Breadcrumb navigation - Add empty port to group input and output nodes to quicken port creation (inspired by Blender) - Smart previews inside groups (use inputs of specific group node clicked to edit the group) - Edit node group directly? - Allow parameter refs at least, consider varyings and parameters (but most likely not) - Add an `active` property to `VisualShaderNodeGroupOutput` so that you can have multiple output nodes and switch between them - Implement expandable ports - Write unit tests

Very exciting! I got a build worked up and did some testing this evening. So far it feels pretty solid. I was able to copy some existing nodes and paste them into a group without much trouble. Creating input and output nodes feels a lot like blender, so you can see the inspiration there.

I feel like it's in pretty good shape! I do think that the feedback posted above by @Delsin-Yu ([here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99404#issuecomment-2890154123)) is still quite valid, particularly the User Experience aspects. But, that said, I personally wouldn't want anything holding this feature back, and could see those as future polish QOL enhancements.

Thank you once again for your hard work on implementing this! I know it's been a huge undertaking, and it's very much appreciated. I'll continue to do more testing over the next couple of weeks and report back with any findings.

Cheers!

# New changes: - Rework group ports dialog partially - Improved port name editing - Add/remove buttons now use icons and tooltip instead of text, hide remove button when the list is empty - You can now reorder ports with the respective move up/down buttons (supports undo) - Use variant type icons for items (even though I hate them ;)) - Fixed handling of sampler ports ## Known issues - The problem with group port changes (removal/reorder) are connections "outside" the group, so in the graphs which contain instances of the group. Updating those connections with proper undo/redo support is pretty complex and expensive. We'd also need to decide whether all graphs (visual shaders or groups) need to be updated, even those not opened, or just the current shader graph stack. - Currently, moving a port does simply not update connections outside the group (to group instances) due to the problems mentioned above.

> @Chaosus Everything you mentioned should now be fixed/implemented.
> 
> Concerning the group input and output nodes: First I had a strict implementation which ensured exactly one input and one output node. However, that came with its own set of problems and was ugly in code. After that I came up with a general solution that allowed multiple(or none) input and output nodes, which simplified things a lot while providing an actual UX benefit. One could argue that multiple output nodes are not really that useful, but I think it has some value (and making an exception would reintroduce the problem I mentioned again). In Blender, you can have multiple output nodes, but only one is active at a time. This makes sense to me: You could build branches in your group, trying things out, and switching between output nodes - basically allowing you to have several versions of your group without any runtime cost, vaguely similar to conditional compilation. Right now, just the first output node is selected and a warning is shown on the group instance node, so this feature needs to be implemented still. But I'd rather do this in a subsequent PR.

@KoBeWi Well, this design clearly separates interface declaration (ports dialog and the [just added] ports section in inspector) from access, group input/output nodes are just accessors with a convenience button to change the interface. This is the same model Blender uses, and I think it's one of the better ones out there and people are used to it. However I don't want to disguise the fact that Unity and Unreal's native material/shader graph systems both combine interface declaration and access. I think each port is defined by exactly one node, which might be more straight-forward, but that's arguable.

I've made a few important changes:
- From now on, adding a group instance node via the editor automatically adds a new node group containing a group input and output node, they are no longer created when setting an empty group 
- Input and output ports can now also be edited in the inspector (without entering the group), not just via the group input/output dialog (this breaks compat with earlier versions of this PR due to changed serialization by using PropertyListHelper)

For an easier review I kept the commits separate, they can be squashed later.
Thanks! This PR has been a long-time coming, so it's exciting to finally have it ready to roll!
